method: Whole-file manual reading of StaTaskScheduler.cs and DualKeyDictionary.cs; truncated dictionary middle explicitly reread lines140..225. Exact-commit downloads matched pinned Git blob IDs.
findings: STA scheduler has one background thread consuming unbounded BlockingCollection<Task>. No queue capacity, admission policy or cancellation-aware disposal. Dispose completes adding and joins without timeout; blocked tasks can block disposal indefinitely.

Dispose invoked from scheduler thread would self-join; no guard exists. QueueTask racing disposal can throw; repeated disposal is not guarded. These are source-level paths, not executed Windows failures.
No Windows message pump or SynchronizationContext setup is present in scheduler loop. STA marking alone is not proof of correct COM reentrancy/async continuation behavior.

TryExecuteTaskInline only admits scheduler thread and does not remove an already queued task from collection. Task execution state may prevent duplicate execution but queued entry retention remains until consumer drains.

DualKeyDictionary uses two ordinary dictionaries with no internal synchronization or custom comparers. Optional-key conflicts under overwrite detach optional key from former owner; Add throws, TryAdd rejects.

Remove(KeyValuePair) forwards to Remove(key), ignoring expected value although Contains(pair) checks it. This can remove a mapping with a different value; source confirms contract mismatch without runtime reproduction.

Primary CopyTo lacks explicit null/negative index guards unlike ValueCollection.CopyTo. Default optional key for value types is a real zero-like key because null checks do not represent absence. Generic optional-key semantics need constrained caller choices.
limits: No original C# tests or Windows runtime executed; no foreign production code adopted.
